bindings.label: A 70-year-old woman has a pink, raised, non-tender lesion with progressive skin discoloration on her left breast for 6 months.
She observed skin discoloration on the left breast 6 months prior, which progressively increased and prompted her to seek medical attention.
Physical examination revealed a single 3 × 3 cm pink, non-tender, raised lesion on the left breast at the 12:00 position.
Medical history includes hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes mellitus, and osteoporosis, with no previous breast health issues or surgeries.

She reported no associated pain, new masses, nipple discharge/retraction, or lymphadenopathy; vital signs were within normal limits, she appeared in no distress, and she tolerated a treatment procedure well without complications.
Biopsy of left breast lesion shows dermal confluent large lymphoid cells and epidermal ulceration
Immunohistochemistry shows Ki-67 95%, CD3/CD4/CD5/BCL2/MUM1/CD30 positive, and cytokeratin/ALK1/MPO negative
Patient has primary cutaneous CD30+ T-cell lymphoproliferative disorder/lymphoma
TCR clonality analysis and systemic staging (PET/CT, LDH, bone marrow, and lymph node evaluation) have not yet been performed
Patient has primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma (pcALCL)
Patient has primary cutaneous anaplastic large cell lymphoma (pcALCL)
Radiologist analysis explicitly favors pcALCL over LyP within the CD30+ cutaneous lymphoproliferative spectrum.
Expert analyses state that systemic lymphoma remains a differential until TCR clonality and systemic staging are completed.
Patient has systemic lymphoma with secondary skin involvement
